subject: Scarcity mediation / urgent dedicated GPU handoff — Solaris AI (DL-4821)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Solaris AI <procurement@solaris.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing sync — Solaris / DL-4821

Hi Priya / Solaris procurement team,

Thanks again for the detailed forecast. You mentioned wanting a reserved pool of 8x A100-equivalent GPUs for Q3 with burst to 12x for steady-state inference. Before we lock sizing in the contract, can you confirm:

- Peak qps and 95th percentile latency SLOs for the production model (tokens/sec and max latency)
- Expected training fine-tuning windows (dates) that might require additional transient capacity
- Whether encryption-at-rest KMS will require private deployment nodes or if hosted dedicated is acceptable

We ran a preliminary right-sizing and there are two things to flag: (1) the Aurora reserved tranche already has commitments that conflict with a straight allocation of 8x for the requested window; (2) the preferred burst dates overlap with Trident Labs’ onboarding batch (deal DL-4678).

If you can send the qps numbers and a prioritized list of peak windows by EOD Monday, we can prepare an allocation proposal and a mediation playbook for the handoff. Attached: a blank commit matrix template.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

Attachment: DL-4821_commit_matrix_template.csv (spreadsheet stub)

From: Solaris AI <procurement@solaris.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Trident Labs <trident-sales@trident.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing sync — Solaris / DL-4821

Hi Karthik,

Thanks — quick answers below and attached a filled matrix. Short version: the peaks are non-negotiable windows tied to customer SLAs and clinical batch runs; Solaris can shift non-critical training but not production inference.

- Peak QPS: 420 qps sustained over 4–6 hour windows; 95th latency target: <= 120ms per request.
- Fine-tuning: two scheduled 24-hour windows (2028-07-09 and 2028-08-14) — can be deferred by up to 72 hours with notice.
- KMS: must use Solaris-managed keys; we need VPC/private deployment nodes (cannot use multi-tenant hosted pools).

We attached DL-4821_proposed_commit_matrix.csv. Let us know if Redwood can map reserved GPUs in a private deployment and guarantee the burst on the given windows.

—Priya Nambiar
Head of Procurement, Solaris AI
procurement@solaris.ai
Attachment: DL-4821_proposed_commit_matrix.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing sync — Solaris / DL-4821

Karthik / Marissa — heads up on Solaris’ KMS requirement and the burst timing. The Aurora tranche (reserved private nodes) is 70% committed for Q3 — current headroom for private VPC nodes is limited. Trident's onboarding (DL-4678) requests a private burst on 2028-07-09 as well (same day as Solaris’ first fine-tune).

Proposed internal options:
- Option A: Prioritize Solaris for private nodes (DL-4821) since their contract is near-final and they require KMS. Move Trident to hosted dedicated or offer deferred burst windows.
- Option B: Offer Solaris a hybrid: base reserved capacity on private nodes but allow burst on hosted dedicated for short windows — has security implications but may be acceptable with additional audit controls.
- Option C: If neither works, propose temporal arbitration: split the burst window into two contiguous blocks and schedule a 50/50 split across customers.

I recommend we run an urgent triage with Ops + Security to confirm feasibility of Option B; otherwise we should escalate to leadership for a decision before Monday.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Account Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity sizing sync — Solaris / DL-4821

Laura — forwarding the thread. Solaris’ KMS/privateness requirement is binding and the first fine-tune/burst date conflicts directly with Trident. Ben outlined three options below. We need a prioritization decision: do we accept the security tradeoffs for Option B or elevate?

Quick context for leadership:
- Impact if we deny Solaris’ private requirement: likely deal slippage (DL-4821) and loss of trust; Solaris is enterprise-tier and procurement signals are strong.
- Impact if we deprioritize Trident: smaller ARR but short-term churn risk; Trident is flexible on timing.

Suggested ask: Laura / VP — decide by Monday EOD to allow us to triage with Ops and issue contract addendum.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Enterprise Sales
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing sync — Solaris / DL-4821

Team — reviewed. High-level position: we should prioritize Solaris (DL-4821) for private node allocation with the following constraints and mitigations:

1) Guardrails: Offer Option B (hybrid) only if Security signs off that Solaris’ KMS can be integrated to the private control plane without exposing keys to hosted pools. If Security cannot sign off within 48 hours, Solaris receives guaranteed private base capacity but bursts are limited to a negotiated schedule (only during low-risk windows).

2) Make Trident (DL-4678) a first-class candidate for offset credits: offer an additional 10% discount on committed months or provide prioritized onboarding for hosted-dedicated lanes to avoid losing the account. Sales must prepare a formal mitigation proposal for Trident by EOD Monday.

3) Ops action: freeze any new private node assignments that would touch the Aurora tranche until we complete this mediation. Ops to provide a capacity and risk memo (by Monday 18:00 PT) outlining reshuffle cost and estimated impact on latency and SLOs.

4) Contract / Legal: prepare a short SLA addendum that reflects the burst carve-outs and audit windows (Laura to coordinate).

Please confirm responsibilities: Ben — lead Ops and Security triage. Marissa — draft Trident mitigation offer. Karthik — lock in Solaris’ final acceptance for our constraints. I’ll join the triage call Monday if needed.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

On Sat, Jun 15, 2028 at 15:04, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Laura — forwarding the thread. Solaris’ KMS/privateness requirement is binding and the first fine-tune/burst date conflicts directly with Trident.

From: Priya Nambiar <procurement@solaris.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scarcity mediation / urgent dedicated GPU handoff — Solaris AI (DL-4821)

Laura / team — thanks for the quick decision and for outlining the guardrails. Solaris can accept the hybrid (Option B) only if the following are explicit in the addendum:

- Private nodes for base reserved capacity must be physically isolated in our VPC and full KMS handoff (Solaris-managed keys).
- Any burst onto hosted-dedicated must be preceded by a 24-hour written notice and is limited to read-only inference workloads (no KV-cache sharing) for up to two 6-hour windows per month.
- Audit logs and network egress reports must be shared weekly for two months following the first burst window.

If Redwood can draft the addendum with those terms, Solaris will sign the contract and commit to the proposed 24-month reserved term. We’ve attached a short SLA request (solarise_sla_request.pdf) with required audit fields.

—Priya
Priya Nambiar
Head of Procurement, Solaris AI
procurement@solaris.ai
Attachment: solarise_sla_request.pdf
